claims: Over 1,000 apps listed with exact prompts to rebuild them
Each app is rated 'yes', 'kinda' or 'not really' (evening project / weekend project / not worth it)
Site shows how much money you would save per app and why you might not want to rebuild it
Creator's advice: only replace apps where cost is high and build time is low
how_to_steps: Go to canivibecodeit.com and search for an app you pay for (e.g. Granola)
Or scroll to trending apps / 'The Death List'
Read the yes/kinda/not-really verdict and estimated savings
Click the app to get the exact rebuild prompt and the reasons not to build it
Paste the prompt into Claude or ChatGPT
on_screen_only: Hero: 'Can I vibecode ___?' with subtitle '1,000 apps, one question each: can AI build you a replacement today, or is it still worth paying for?'
'The Death List' table with app names (Granola, Notion and others), monthly price column, green/red verdict badges
Detail page 'Can I vibecode Granola?' with a green 'YES' badge and savings per month, a long prompt block and a 'why you might not' section with red arrow
cta: Try it and comment which app you replace; follow

relevance.why: Useful two ways for a founder: cutting SaaS spend, and as a cheap market-research list of which apps are now trivially cloneable (i.e. which markets are commoditising).

implement_score.why: Rebuilding tools you pay for usually costs more founder time than the subscription; skim the Death List for ideas and for the prompt structures, but do not spend evenings cloning Granola.

verify: Who runs canivibecodeit.com and are the prompts/savings numbers curated or auto-generated?
Are the verdicts honest about maintenance burden (hosting, auth, syncing)?
Check the site's monetisation (affiliate links, lead-gen)
